transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood) — Mia, Evan, Sanjay, Leah (Pacifica)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Dr. Mia Torres: Mia here, hi.
[00:06] Evan Brooks: Evan here.
[00:07] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, present.
[00:09] Leah Kim: Leah as well.
[00:11] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Cool. So agenda — quick renewal recap, talk through expansion asks (capacity + region), security items, and agree next steps. Priya, do you want to take the capacity piece?
[00:21] Priya Nair: Yeah sure. Hey, um, so from the usage data we've seen over the last 90 days Pacifica's baseline is, uh, about 10 p50 concurrent inference pipelines with spikes to 28 during morning window. The proposal we discussed internally for a reserved plan is 3x A40-equivalent GPUs — that gives you the headroom for the spikes and room for new models. We also recommended enabling the prefix/KV cache for frequent clinical prompts which should reduce token compute by, like, 18-25% depending on prompt reuse.
[00:50] Evan Brooks: Sorry can I interrupt — when you say A40, do you mean the dedicated pool option or the hosted accelerated instance?
[00:57] Priya Nair: Good question. This is for Redwood Dedicated — reserved capacity. Hosted would be the shared multi-tenant offering, which is more elastic but doesn't guarantee the same steady throughput. For a clinical SLA and predictable latency we think Dedicated is the right fit.
[01:12] Dr. Mia Torres: We need predictable tail latency — some of these inference calls are part of our triage flow, so 99th percentile matters.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Yup, totally. That's why the dedicated pool with a pinned count plus the smart routing helps maintain tail SLA. Also, we can do regional pinning — which leads to the US-West ask.
[01:29] Leah Kim: Right, about that — we're expanding a clinic network on the West Coast and they want lower latency to West Coast region. Is that a separate charge or can we repurpose capacity?
[01:38] Priya Nair: We can either add a multi-region addon — which provisions an additional dedicated pool in us-west with some routing rules — or route traffic from us-west to existing region with a slightly higher latency. Multi-region will be additional cost (we price per reserved pool), but it gives you redundancy and lower tail latency.
[01:56] Evan Brooks: What's the expected delta on pricing for adding us-west?
[01:59] Jordan Lee: Ballpark, for a second reserved pool of the same size it's roughly 70% of the first pool price under our term discounts — because of committed volume. We'll put exact numbers in the quote.
[02:12] Sanjay Patel: On security, important Q — can the us-west pool be in our VPC? We need traffic staying on private networking for PHI. Also need KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:22] Priya Nair: Yes, with Redwood Private we can deploy the control plane in your VPC and the inference nodes in your private subnets. KMS/HSM integrations are supported — we have integrations with AWS KMS and customer-managed HSMs. Audit logs and request-level tracing are exportable to your logging stack.
[02:37] Leah Kim: Any limitation on model variants when running in private? We rely on some optimized quantized checkpoints.
[02:42] Priya Nair: Generally supported — we do need to validate specific kernels and quantization profiles for your model family. There might be a short onboarding window to run compatibility tests, but no blockers expected.
[02:53] Dr. Mia Torres: Can you say more about the KV-cache you mentioned? Is that safe for PHI — are we ever storing patient content in cache?
[03:00] Priya Nair: Good callout. KV-cache is an ephemeral inference cache — by default it stores model key/value state in memory per inference node. For PHI we recommend configuring cache policies that never persist to disk and setting retention to session-only; in Private deployments you can also control cache isolation. We'll include recommended settings in the security appendix.
[03:20] Evan Brooks: Cool. For the pilot we want to run our clinical triage model with 500 concurrent sessions for a 48-hour window, end-to-end — can Redwood support that as a temporary burst?
[03:30] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have burst capacity options. For Dedicated customers we can provision temporary burst capacity — it'll be priced as a short-term add-on. For the pilot, we can schedule the burst to be live during your test window.
[03:41] Sanjay Patel: Regarding compliance, what about SOC 2 scope and penetration testing reports? We need evidence for our security team.
[03:48] Jordan Lee: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary under NDA. I'll attach the current artifacts to the follow-up email.
[03:56] Leah Kim: And contract-wise — we're looking at a 24-month extension if we move to Dedicated with a multi-region option. Any discount breakpoints?
[04:04] Jordan Lee: Yes, term discounts apply — 12, 24, 36 month tiers. For 24 months with the reserved commitment you're likely to see a 12-18% discount on list, plus we can roll region add-on pricing into the committed spend to improve economics. We'll put several term options in the quote.
[04:20] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[04:23] Priya Nair: One more technical detail — for model rollout strategies, we recommend canarying the new us-west pool with traffic shaping (10/20/50) and fall back to the primary region if latency breaches threshold. The routing policy is configurable in the Console.
[04:40] Evan Brooks: Any telemetry we can get during the pilot? Token-level cost breakdown would be great.
[04:44] Priya Nair: Yep, Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces. We'll enable an additional retention window for logs for the pilot if you want longer term analysis.
[04:55] Dr. Mia Torres: If we sign for 24 months and add the region, what's the earliest we can go live? We're aiming for September 1st for the West Coast clinics.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Assuming contract sign by mid-August and we clear the security checklist quickly, the provisioning and onboarding target of ~2 weeks per region is realistic — so early Sept is achievable. We'll calendar resources once terms are agreed.
[05:16] Evan Brooks: I want to flag an integration detail — our observability expects OpenTelemetry traces; does Redwood export compatible spans?
[05:22] Priya Nair: Yes, we export OTEL spans and have a tracing hook to forward to your collector. We'll share the sample config.
[05:30] Leah Kim: A small question on data retention — we need logs retained for 1 year for audit. Is that possible?
[05:35] Jordan Lee: Yes, we offer extended observability retention as an add-on. For Private customers we can also route logs to your S3 bucket or logging endpoint so you control retention.
[05:44] Sanjay Patel: Encryption at rest — all model artifacts and inputs encrypted?
[05:48] Priya Nair: At rest encryption is enforced — KMS-backed keys for model checkpoints and customer data. For extra control you can bring your own key.
[05:55] Dr. Mia Torres: Great. Any risks we should watch for?
[05:58] Jordan Lee: Main risks are onboarding validation for quantized kernels and the legal timeline — if compliance review drags it could push provisioning. We'll mitigate by running compatibility tests in parallel with the security review.
[06:10] Evan Brooks: Sounds good. Let's talk brief pricing outline — Jordan?
[06:13] Jordan Lee: Sure. High level: baseline reserved pool (3x) — list price X, with 24-month commits discount brings it to ~Y; second regional pool at ~70% of first pool subject to commit; pilot burst priced separately as one-time add-on. Exact numbers in quote.
[06:27] Leah Kim: We'll need line items separated for Dedicated, Private (VPC), and add-ons — security docs, retention, pilot burst.
[06:34] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll send detailed quote with three scenarios.
[06:38] Dr. Mia Torres: Next steps for us: internal legal + security to review artifacts, Evan to coordinate pilot dataset, and Jordan to send quote.
[06:46] Jordan Lee: Perfect — we'll follow up. Any final questions?
[06:50] Sanjay Patel: Can you include the SLA matrix in the follow-up? 99th p answer latency for Dedicated vs Hosted.
[06:55] Jordan Lee: Yes, SLA matrix will be included.
[06:58] Evan Brooks: Thanks all.
[07:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the quote by Friday.

Meeting end.
